{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Marion Lee Johnson''' is an American mathematician whose work was crucial to the landing of the [[Apollo 11]] mission. She was a mathematician on the [[Boeing]]/[[NASA]] team, where she worked in preparing data for the vehicle impact trajectories.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Marion Lee Johnson|url=https://www.cincymuseum.org/marion-lee-johnson/|access-date=2020-07-12|website=Cincinnati Museum Center|language=en-US}}</ref> Her perfect score over 20 successful missions earned her a place on the Apollo/Saturn V Roll of Honor.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|last=Golden Carmon|first=Rev. W.|date=May 15, 2017|title=Marion Lee Johnson: A Hidden Figure|url=https://www.thechristianrecorder.com/marion-lee-johnson-a-hidden-figure/|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=October 8, 2019|website=The Christian Recorder}}</ref><ref name=":0" />

After completion of the project, she worked for [[Pfizer]] for 26 years. She currently lives in New Jersey.

== Life and career   ==
She was born in a working-class family in [[Savannah, Georgia|Savannah]], [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]], with three sisters and a brother.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web|last=Journal|first=Caitlin Mota {{!}} The Jersey|date=2017-02-26|title=Jersey City teacher honored as one of N.J.'s own 'Hidden Figures'|url=https://www.nj.com/hudson/2017/02/jersey_city_woman_honored_as_one_of_njs_own_hidden.html|access-date=2020-07-12|website=nj|language=en}}</ref> She attended school at Moses Jackson, in a segregated neighborhood. Very early, she fell in love with mathematics, and credits this love to her 7th grade maths teacher, Walter B. Simmons.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=Monks|first=Michael|title='Hidden Figure' Marion Lee Johnson Talks NASA Career|url=https://www.wvxu.org/post/hidden-figure-marion-lee-johnson-talks-nasa-career|access-date=2020-07-12|website=www.wvxu.org|date=18 February 2020|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=NJ's own 'Hidden Figure' delivers powerful speech on the importance of mentoring {{!}} Video|url=https://www.njtvonline.org/news/video/njs-hidden-figure-delivers-powerful-speech-importance-mentoring/|access-date=2020-07-12|website=NJTV News|language=en-US}}</ref> She graduated class valedictorian from high school at [[Tompkins High School|Thompkins High School]] in 1963.<ref name=Bluffton>{{Cite web|url=https://www.blufftontoday.com/news/2018-02-13/savannah-s-own-hidden-figure-marion-lee-johnson-worked-apollo-11-program|title=Savannah's own 'Hidden Figure': Marion Lee Johnson worked on Apollo 11 program|last=Segedy|first=Andria|website=Bluffton Today|language=en|access-date=2019-10-08}}</ref><ref name=":4" /> In 1967, she was granted a scholarship at [[Talladega College]] in Talladega, [[Alabama]], to study mathematics,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://newyork.cbslocal.com/2018/02/01/black-history-marion-lee-johnson/|title=Black History Month One-On-One: 'Hidden Figure' Marion Lee Johnson|date=2018-02-01|language=en-US|access-date=2019-10-08}}</ref> and assumed that her degree would lead her to become a teacher.<ref name=":1" /> After losing her scholarship because her grades had slipped, Johnson took out a loan to continue her degree, and prioritised her studies in order to requalify for the scholarship.<ref name=":5" />

After graduation, at the age of 21, she went to work as an associate engineer at Boeing Company in [[Huntsville, Alabama]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|date=2018-02-01|title=Black History Month One-On-One: 'Hidden Figure' Marion Lee Johnson|url=https://newyork.cbslocal.com/2018/02/01/black-history-marion-lee-johnson/|access-date=2020-07-12|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":4" /><ref name=":6" /> She was assigned to the Launch Systems branch of the Boeing/NASA team at the Marshall Space Flight Centre to prepare the landing of the Apollo 11 mission.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":4" /> At the time, very few women worked at the Space Flight Centre.<ref name=":2" /> Johnson worked under the supervision of [[Arthur Rudolph]] and rocket designer [[Wernher von Braun]], on the calculations to simulate vehicle piece impact trajectories (where the booster rockets would fall).<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":4" /><ref name=":6">{{Cite web|date=2017-03-29|title=Here and Now on March 26, 2017: Marion Johnson|url=https://abc7ny.com/1815282/|access-date=2020-07-12|website=ABC7 New York|language=en}}</ref> According to Lee, Boeing was a diverse place. In an interview for 1010 WINS' with Larry Mullins in 2018, she said: "You had a lot of people there - a lot of people from all different cultures - and we all worked together."<ref name=":3" /> According to Johnson, it was only after seeing the 2016 movie [[Hidden Figures]] that she realised how important her own contributions were to NASA.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mathematician and Engineer Marion Johnson, of the Apollo 11 Mission, Inspires Girl Scouts to Become America's Next Tech Leaders|url=https://www.tapinto.net/towns/new-brunswick/articles/mathematician-and-engineer-marion-johnson-of-the-1|access-date=2020-07-12|website=TAPinto|language=en}}</ref>

After two years working for Boeing/NASA, Johnson then went to work at Pfizer, Inc., where she became Project Leader for the Corporate Information Technology Division.<ref name=":4" /> She retired from Pfizer after 26 years.<ref name=":4" />

A resident of [[Union County, New Jersey]], she recently retired from [[Branford Hall Career Institute]] as a Computer Networking and Security Instructor.<ref name="Bluffton" /> The city of Plainfield awarded Johnson the key to the city, and designated two days to honor her legacy.<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=Marion Lee Johnson Day - City of Plainfield|url=https://www.cjadeltas.org/event/marion-lee-johnson-day-city-plainfield/|access-date=2020-07-12|website=Central Jersey Alumnae Chapter of Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Incorporated|language=en-US}}</ref> She is married to J. Frank Johnson, the owner of an accounting, tax, audit, and advisory services company, with whom she has three children.<ref name=":4" />
